main_text.l: SUBSECTIO SECUNDA
De Subactione Monarchiæ regno Christi ad-
versariæ
Analysis.
ONtinuatur hinc porrò fermo Dei, atque
pergit à judicio Judæorum (qui se
subduxerant) ad judicium gentium, sub
insigni monarchatu se præconio regni
Christi opponentium; quæ duo judicia hic loci ita inter se
comparantur, ut etiam tanquam proximè cohærentia
connectantur: quam comparationem excutiemus ad
verf. 5. Hinc facilè colligimus subsequentium rerum
argumentum non posse referri ad tempora præconium
testis istius veracis fidemque adstipulantium anteceden-
tia: sed necessario spectare ad tempus regni Christi, à
quo ecclesia credentium in Christum fuit collecta. Ab-
errant enim à sermonis tenore isti Interpretes, qui ne-
scio quo saltu retrogradò hic ad tempora monarchiæ Ba-
bylonicæ resiliunt: comparatur enim Monarcha aliquis
perfidus, in visione oblatus, respectu judicii perferen-
di, cum Judæis, ob subductionem supplicio affectis:
unde sequitur prioris judicium post illud Judæorum fuisse
exspectandum. Apponimus hic, quæ Cl. Coccejus
habet in commentario suo. „ Hanc descriptionem judi-
candi (inquit) multi interpretes accommodant Baby-
lonio. Sed patet, aut eodem, aut etiam majori jure ac-
commodari posse Romano. Edenda igitur est ratio,
quare

page.notes: The first word is a large decorated initial "C" followed by "ONtinuatur"; the printed word is "Continuatur", the initial C is shown as a woodcut and joined to the word, so it is written here as "Continuatur" with the first letter restored. The "Aaa 2" line is a gathering signature and is shown in the foot element. The left-margin bullet and the text "quare" at the foot are catchword and printed marks. Several italic and quoted words are in the printed original; the opening quotation mark before "Hanc" is printed. Some characters at the right edge of the scan are faint and were read with confidence only where legible.
